records.text: Sarah Tewell said she saw a shot hit Charlie Kirk in the chest and blood gush from where his heart was.
records.speaker: Sarah Tewell

appearances.snippet: So basically I heard a loud bang which I figured a shot would be a little bit louder but I just saw it hit him in the chest and then all of a sudden just tons of blood gushing right out where his heart is and then he like fell over and slumped down and everybody got down and was screaming and then we all ran.

verification.notes: Transcript context reviewed. Archived local-news footage records Sara Tewell saying she saw the impact in the chest and blood where the heart was. This verifies what the witness said; it does not validate her anatomical interpretation made immediately after a traumatic event.

verification.notes: Transcript context reviewed. Archived local-news footage records Sara Tewell saying she personally believed Kirk was dead on impact. This verifies the attributed opinion, not a medical determination of time of death.

records.text: In a later interview, Sarah Tewell said Charlie Kirk was shot in the neck and that she believed he was dead on impact, although she had heard he was in critical condition.
records.speaker: Sarah Tewell

appearances.snippet: And that is when Charlie Kirk was shot. It was in the neck and I watched the blood just spurt out all over his body as he slumped over and fell down. I believe that he was dead on impact, but it sounds like he is in critical condition.

verification.notes: Transcript context reviewed. The archived later KSL interview records Sara Tewell describing a neck wound, saying she believed Kirk was dead on impact, and acknowledging that she had heard he was in critical condition.

records.text: Sarah Tewell said the shot entered Charlie Kirk's left side from her right and estimated the shooter was about 200 yards away.
records.speaker: Sarah Tewell

appearances.snippet: Yes, correct. Yeah, it went right into his left side and the shooter was from my right and even in the middle it was still to the right. And I'm pretty sure you had somebody say this earlier, but I think it was about 200 yards away.

verification.notes: Transcript context reviewed. Archived interview footage records Tewell saying the shot entered on the left side, came from her right, and was roughly 200 yards away. This verifies her attributed account, not the objective trajectory or distance.

links.title: Account Change Does Not Prove Coaching

records.text: Owens said it was remarkable that Tewell's account shifted from a hit directly to the heart to a hit on the left side of the neck.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: That is remarkable. That is remarkable. Directly to his heart to now on the left side of his neck. But she wasn't done.

verification.notes: Transcript context reviewed. Archived clips of the two same-day interviews document the change from Tewell describing a chest or heart impact to describing a neck impact. Owens accurately identified that discrepancy; the evidence does not establish why the stressed eyewitness used different wording.

links.title: Toole Shift Cast as Cover-Story Evidence

records.text: Owens asserted that witness Sarah Tewell changed her story three times.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: It's a rabbit hole regarding the Sarah Tewell witness—Sarah Tewell—who changed her story three times. We will have that information for you tomorrow.

verification.notes: Available interview excerpts show a material inconsistency: an early account described a hit to the heart or chest, while a later account and the ABC interview described a neck wound. That supports saying the account changed at least once. The reviewed record shows three interviews or versions, not three distinct changes, so the numeric claim is overstated.

records.text: Owens said Sarah Tewell changed her account three times, first saying she saw Charlie Kirk struck in the chest and later saying he was struck in the neck.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: People like Sarah Tewell, the young woman that we showed you who changed her story three times, definitively saw him get hit in the chest, gave a description of how he was bleeding. ... Then said, no, no, he was hit in the neck.

verification.notes: Live searches found secondary commentary and an episode synopsis asserting that an eyewitness first said chest and later neck, but no complete set of three authenticated Sarah Tewell accounts was located. Without the original interviews or a reliable compilation, the claimed three changes cannot be verified.
